title: Repo-wide guard against committed secrets and operator identifiers
description:
aro shipped a repo-scan test scoped to cloud/factory (no token literal, no hash record, FACTORY_TOKEN_HASH absent from wrangler.toml). This is a public repo and that guard should cover the whole tree, including .tick/ — where this run demonstrated the failure mode by writing an operator's cloud account id into committed tick notes.

Add one guard that fails CI on: high-entropy token-shaped literals (tkf_*, PBKDF2 records, GitHub PAT prefixes, Cloudflare/Doppler token prefixes), 32-hex cloud account identifiers, and non-example.com email addresses in tracked files. Scan .tick/ (issues + activity.jsonl) as well as source. Provide a narrow, documented allowlist for the pre-existing hits on main (internal/tickboard/cloud/client_test.go and .tick/issues/xps.json both carry a real operator email) rather than rewriting public history — and make the allowlist entries individually justified so it cannot become a dumping ground.

Wire it into .github/workflows/ci.yml. While you are in that file: there is no job covering cloud/factory at all (flagged by n3e) — add one mirroring the existing 'worker' job with working-directory cloud/factory and cache-dependency-path cloud/factory/pnpm-lock.yaml, or the whole new bundle is unguarded on main.
acceptance_criteria: The guard fails on a deliberately planted account id, token literal, and non-example.com email in a tracked file (including one planted in a .tick/ note), and passes on the clean tree with its documented allowlist. CI runs it. A cloud/factory job exists in ci.yml and passes.
